pros: Rich and ergonomic cabin: Leatherette dashboard, door pads, and steering wheel feel premium, and multiple physical dials help usability.
Great practicality: Adjustable front cupholders, big door pockets with a dustbin and umbrella slots, dual gloveboxes, rear removable storage box ensure more than adequate storage spaces.
Great highway cruiser: Sits at triple-digit speeds effortlessly with enough performance for overtakes.
Premium Features: Massaging and ventilated seats with memory function, 13-speaker Canton audio system, dual wireless phone chargers and three-zone climate control.
cons: Third row space: Only adequate for kids or pets.
Squeaking sounds from a few panels inside after covering 20,000 km+.

pros: Elegant styling: Individual elements in connected LED lighting and illuminated Skoda wordmark at the rear looks chic
Boot space: Not the biggest on-paper, but very practical in real life
Performance: Both 1-litre and 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engines offer good performance
Driving dynamics: Feels fun to drive without any big compromise in ride comfort
Value: Base variants offer a really good functional and convenience feature package
cons: No ADAS features could be a miss for people who do long intercity trips
Rear-view camera: Really poor quality and no dynamic guidelines render it almost useless in anything other than broad daylight
Powertrain options: No CNG, diesel or hybrid powertrain option for people looking for low-running costs

Enough features: Sunroof, ventilated and powered front seats, 10.1-inch touchscreen.
446-litre boot space is more than sufficient for 4 cabin-sized trolley bags.
Fun-to-drive: 1-litre TSI engine is fun to push hard and puts a smile on your face.
cons: No diesel or CNG options available.
Fuel efficiency isn’t great, particularly in heavy city traffic. Expect 10kmpl at best.
Minor annoyances: poor camera quality, very light horn, and noisy seat ventilation blowers spoil the experience.
